missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-model-comparison-C003 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance is not supplied for every assertion in the entry. The theorem asserts (handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex lines 136-137) that declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general. That is a claim that something fails in general, and no witness or argument for it appears in the annex proof (handbook/annex/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex lines 97-104 prove only invariance under the transported prior and then restate scope) or anywhere in the body. Every other 'need not' claim in this chapter gets an explicit counterexample in its annex item. A secondary point: in the intrinsic weight identity, the claim that {sum_k alpha_k r_k > 0} has full Q_alpha-mass is asserted after 'similarly' (annex lines 84-85) with no written step.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-model-comparison-C003 (partial): This entry's 'construction or argument' and 'worked boundary' are not supplied for its parameter-coordinate direction, and neither is the full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance). The statement (handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex lines 136-137) asserts that declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is in general not a transport. Neither the body nor the declared proof gives an argument, counterexample or worked case for this. Annex lines 97-104 prove only the transported (positive) case and then restate the restriction ('not under an arbitrary reassignment of a coordinate density'). This is a missing promised direction/case. The only witness in the handbook is thm:p15-bayes-transformation (handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex lines 314-319). It belongs to another unit, is not cross-referenced from this entry, and concerns posterior means rather than the marginal likelihood m_k, so it cannot be credited here.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-model-comparison-C003 (partial): The declared status proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance promises a full proof, but one promised case has none. At body lines 136-137 of handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex the entry says 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general'. The declared proof (handbook/annex/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex lines 97-104) proves only that m_k(x) is unchanged when the prior and likelihood are pushed forward, then restates the negative ('not under an arbitrary reassignment of a coordinate density') with no argument and no counterexample. Neither the entry nor its proof cites the uniform-prior/theta-squared counterexample that exists separately at handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex lines 313-318. The failure condition 'missing promised direction/case' holds. The rest of the entry is proved at annex lines 59-113, and the worked boundary is at body 148-155 / annex 115-119.

sections.title: Model averaging, label refinement and uncertainty decomposition

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-model-comparison-C003 (partial): The full treatment promised by proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance lacks any argument or worked boundary for the theorem's stated negative coordinate claim (handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex 136-137: 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general'). The declared annex item proves only the transported case (handbook/annex/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex 97-102). It then restates the negative claim (annex 103-104) without a counterexample or derivation. The worked example after the theorem (body 148-155) concerns density versions at a null point, not parameter coordinates. A suitable instance exists in thm:p15-bayes-transformation (handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex 313-319; annex 372-392), but this theorem and its proof never cite it. Every other element of C003 is present: the version change, the intrinsic Q_* comparison via RN uniqueness, d nu' = h d nu, parameter transport, the observation bijection and the null-point example.
